rows.selection_reason: 1) Evidence/uncertainty: No experiments have been completed, so there is zero information about which modality, encoder, profile strategy, or fusion method performs best. The most critical unknown is the performance floor—how well the simplest possible model does. 2) What this tests: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most minimal, interpretable baseline in the search space. It isolates the RNA signal with the most basic linear encoder (PCA to 2000 dims) and a single profile, removing all confounding complexity from learned encoders, multi-profile aggregation, or cross-modal fusion. 3) Why it is the best first use of budget: Establishing this anchor is essential before any comparative conclusion can be drawn. It is also the cheapest configuration to train (no learned image encoder, no transformer aggregation, no fusion), preserving compute for subsequent experiments. Once this floor is known, the next experiments can efficiently test whether (a) image modality adds value, (b) richer RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) improve over PCA, and (c) multimodal fusion outperforms either single modality—each a high-uncertainty, high-impact design question that this baseline makes interpretable.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), we have essentially no information about whether the image modality contributes useful signal. The most critical structural question is whether multimodal fusion improves over the RNA-only baseline. Config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is a minimal, controlled extension of config_001: it keeps the same RNA encoder and profile setting, and adds only the image branch with the simplest fusion (concat). This directly answers 'does adding image information help?' If accuracy jumps substantially, we know to invest subsequent budget in multimodal variants (better encoders, multiprofile, weighted fusion). If it stays near 0.485, we know the image modality (at least with ResNet-50) is not the bottleneck and should pivot to improving the RNA side (multiprofile, scvi/scgpt encoders). This single experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about the highest-leverage design axis under a limited budget.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) achieved 0.527 acc / 0.510 F1, a meaningful +4.2% improvement over the RNA-only baseline (config_001, 0.485/0.464), confirming that adding the image modality is beneficial. However, we have zero data on whether multiprofile (capturing multiple spatial profiles per cell) provides additional signal over singleprofile. This is the largest unexplored design axis. config_018 is the minimal logical extension of config_016: it keeps the same model setting (multimodal), RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion (concat), changing only the profile setting to multiprofile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool). This isolates the effect of multiprofile while minimizing confounding variables (no new encoder, no new fusion method, no complex aggregation). Under a tight budget, resolving whether multiprofile adds value is the highest-information experiment: if it helps, it unlocks a large family of improved configs; if it does not, we can rule out that axis and focus on fusion method or encoder choice next.

Evidence: The largest performance gain so far came from switching to multi-profile with avgpool aggregation (config_018: 0.619 acc vs config_016: 0.527 acc, +9.2 pp), confirming that multi-profile aggregation is a critical design axis. However, we have only tested one aggregation strategy (avgpool) and one fusion strategy (concat). Uncertainty: It is unclear whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) that can model inter-profile relationships will outperform simple averaging, or whether the current avgpool is already near-optimal for this task. This experiment (config_020) tests transformer aggregation while holding all other variables constant (PCA, ResNet50, concat, multi-profile), providing a clean ablation of the aggregation choice. It is the best use of the next budget slot because it directly extends the current best configuration along the most impactful design axis (multi-profile aggregation), and the result will inform whether to invest further in transformer-based architectures or pivot to other dimensions (e.g., weighted fusion, ViT-L image encoder).

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the clear best at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1, showing that multiprofile+avgpool is a strong recipe. However, all multimodal results so far used concat fusion; the weighted-fusion alternative is completely untested. Question: config_019 is identical to config_018 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, giving a clean one-variable A/B test of whether learned/adaptive modality weighting outperforms simple concatenation. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) it directly exploits the strongest configuration found so far, (2) it isolates a single high-impact design choice (how modalities are combined) with zero confounds, (3) the answer generalizes—knowing whether weighted fusion helps or hurts informs every future multimodal configuration, and (4) under a tight budget, a controlled comparison against the current best is more informative than jumping to a second untested variable (e.g., a new image encoder or RNA encoder) where the result would be harder to attribute.

Evidence: The current best configuration (config_019: multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves acc=0.639, and we have strong evidence that multiprofile + avgpool + weighted fusion is the optimal architecture for the resnet50 image encoder. However, the image encoder choice (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) is a major untested design dimension — we have only ever used resnet50. Question: config_025 tests whether upgrading the image encoder to a larger, ImageNet-pretrained ViT-L (while holding the otherwise-best multiprofile/avgpool/weighted/pca_n2000 settings constant) yields a meaningful accuracy gain over resnet50. Why this is the best next experiment: It is a single-variable exploitation of the strongest evidence (config_019) along the most impactful untested axis. A positive result opens a new performance ceiling; a null result tells us resnet50 is sufficient and shifts focus to the RNA encoder or other factors. This is more informative than testing transformer+weighted (config_021), where the 4-point gap between avgpool and transformer under concat makes a reversal under weighted unlikely.

The current best config (config_019: PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.639 acc. Key evidence shows multiprofile and weighted fusion are strong, avgpool beats transformer, and image encoder choice (ResNet50 vs ViT-L) makes negligible difference. The major untested axis is the RNA encoder: all experiments so far use PCA (a simple linear projection). config_031 (scvi_n200, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) is a clean single-variable change from config_019, isolating whether a learned nonlinear RNA representation (scVI latent) can outperform PCA. This is the highest-value uncertainty to resolve: if scvi_n200 improves performance, it opens a productive exploration direction for RNA encoders; if not, it confirms PCA is sufficient and we can focus budget on other axes. Under a limited budget, this experiment maximally reduces uncertainty about an important design choice while maintaining all other settings at their empirically validated best values.

The strongest single-factor improvement in the history is the RNA encoder upgrade from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (config_019→config_031: 0.639→0.678 acc), suggesting that learned RNA representations are the most impactful design axis. The current best (config_031: scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) has not yet been compared against scgpt, another learned/generative RNA encoder. config_043 is a clean single-variable swap (scvi_n200→scgpt) holding all other settings at their validated best (multiprofile, resnet50, avgpool, weighted). This directly tests whether the RNA encoder axis can be pushed further or whether scvi_n200 already captures most of the benefit of learned encodings. Given that the RNA encoder produced the largest observed gain (~4 acc points), resolving whether scgpt offers additional improvement is the highest-information experiment: if scgpt wins, it opens a new optimization direction; if it ties or loses, it confirms scvi_n200 as the ceiling on this axis and redirects budget toward image encoder or aggregation refinements.

Evidence: config_031 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) is the current best at 0.678 acc, clearly outperforming pca_n2000 (0.639) and scgpt (0.525) under identical settings. The avgpool+weighted aggregation/fusion combo is well-supported by multiple experiments. The remaining uncertainty in this top pipeline is the image encoder choice: with pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l (0.635) was marginally below resnet50 (0.639), but the interaction with scvi_n200 is untested. Question: Does imagenet_vit_l complement scvi_n200 better than resnet50, potentially pushing past 0.678? Why this is best: config_037 is a clean single-variable change (image encoder only) from the current best, directly testing the most important remaining design decision in the top-performing pipeline. It either yields a new best or confirms resnet50 sufficiency, reducing uncertainty efficiently under the limited budget.

The current best configuration (config_037: scvi_n200 + ViT + avgpool + weighted, 0.7062 acc) was reached through a consistent pattern: multiprofile >> singleprofile, avgpool > transformer (config_018 vs 020), weighted > concat (config_019 vs 018), scvi_n200 >> PCA >> scgpt, and ViT > ResNet with scvi_n200. The key remaining uncertainty for this top-performing combination is whether the avgpool-over-transformer finding generalizes to the scvi_n200 + ViT setting. Config_039 (scvi_n200 + ViT + transformer + weighted) directly tests this by changing only the aggregation from the current best. If avgpool still wins, it confirms the aggregation choice is robust across encoders and we can confidently lock in the architecture. If transformer unexpectedly performs comparably or better, it would indicate that the richer scvi+ViT features benefit from attention-based aggregation, opening a new optimization direction. This is the highest-information single experiment: it exploits the strongest direction while reducing uncertainty about a core architectural choice, making it the best use of the next budget slot.
